# BuffRadar

[![CI](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

BuffRadar is a focused click-to-buff queue for **WoW: Forever** (Interface
16001): see nearby players missing a buff you know, then click a name or press
**Cast next buff**. Your character goes first by default. The queue is the main
thing; optional controls stay out of the way until you want them.

## Safe, smart, streamlined

- **Simple core loop:** one small queue, one click or keypress. Turn on Simple
  Mode to hide advanced settings without changing your buff choices.
- **More control than a minimal buff list:** compared with Manners, BuffRadar
  adds optional sorting by role, distance, or need; per-buff rebuff thresholds;
  and a persistent ignore list. Use only the controls that help your group.
- **Safety first:** casts use secure game buttons and stop during combat
  lockdown. City, battleground, and flight-path pauses are available when you
  want them. The read-only status bridge cannot cast or change settings.

The [Forever Player Guide](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/editions/forever/README.md) describes the current
workflow. See [TESTING.md](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/TESTING.md) for automated evidence, the event/timer
audit, and the explicit live-client verification status; the detailed
[field-test protocol](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/docs/FIELD_TEST.md) is available for in-game validation.
Release history and feature details are in the
[changelog](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/editions/forever/CHANGELOG.md) and [feature reference](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/editions/forever/FEATURES.md).

## Find Settings and Actions

Open **Actions** in Settings or use `/br actions` to browse inspection,
management, and troubleshooting tools. Search by name, purpose, or slash command,
and filter results to All, Settings, or Actions. Each action shows its command
and availability; unavailable actions explain the reason and remain readable
with keyboard navigation and narration.

Actions open the existing screens and review steps for assignments, profiles,
preparation, peer status, support reports, and themes. **Why This Buff?** asks
for a player name. The optional Actions keybind or Shift-left-click on the
gear opens the same menu. Existing slash commands and ordinary gear clicks
remain available.

## Optional Coverage Views and Supplies

`/br matrix` opens a read-only player-by-buff coverage grid. Player and buff
pages keep the view bounded; select a player to explain their eligibility.
`/br selfstrip` toggles a separate fixed-position personal buff status display.
Its symbols show confirmed (`+`), missing (`!`), unknown (`?`) and not applicable
(`-`). These are observations, not the header's tracking toggles or cast buttons.
Paused/stale evidence is explicitly marked and never presented as fresh absence.

`/br supplies` opens optional reagent restocking. It starts disabled with no
targets. Enter a supported reagent item ID and a target quantity (0 removes
the target), then set copper and item caps. At a merchant, **Refresh Preview**
lists safe purchases. **Confirm Next Purchase** authorizes only the first
listed reagent row. A new review is required before another purchase; an API
request is reported as pending, not proof that the items arrived.

Quotes are invalidated by merchant, inventory, money or combat changes.
Extended-currency items and unreadable API results are refused. Purchases round
down to whole merchant bundles, honor stock/gold/target limits, and conservatively
use empty general bag slots without assuming spare capacity in existing stacks.
Opening a panel, changing settings and visiting a merchant never buys anything.
The view and restock controls are also available in **Settings → Readiness**.

## Download and Install

1. Download the Forever ZIP from the [latest GitHub release](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/releases/latest)
   or the [CurseForge project](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/buffradar).
2. Extract the `BuffRadar` folder into your Forever client's `Interface/AddOns`
   folder. The installed TOC should be at `Interface/AddOns/BuffRadar/BuffRadar.toc`.
3. Enable BuffRadar in the game's AddOns list. `/br selftest` reports the
   installed version and client interface. This package needs Interface 16001;
   loading it as out of date on another interface does not enable casting.

## Quick Start

- Run `/br plates` to enable friendly nameplates for nearby players outside
  your group. BuffRadar also checks your group, target, and mouseover. Use
  `/br plates names` to keep detection without friendly health bars, or
  `/br plates restore` to undo recorded nameplate changes.
- Click a row to buff its player. Use `/br key` to set keybinds or run
  `/br macro` outside combat to create a cast-next macro for your action bar.
  On a controller, use `/br gamepad` to bind **Cast next buff** directly or
  activate the macro from your action bar.
- Open settings with `/br config`. Run `/br wizard` or Shift-right-click
  the minimap button to choose your activity and role and review a starting
  setup. Use `/br why <name>` for a player's eligibility and assignment.
- Click **?** on the buff window or run `/br nearby` to check friendly
  nameplates, the last scan count, and your current target's eligibility.
- Find settings across all six tabs with `/br config find`. Select a
  `Tab > Setting` result to open its tab and focus the control; selecting
  a result does not change its value. Use Previous/Next for more matches
  and Escape to close search.

## Features

[Live Buff Queue](#live-buff-queue) · [Casting](#casting) ·
[Supported Buffs](#supported-buffs) · [Assignments](#assignments) ·
[Raid Tools and Reports](#raid-tools-and-reports) ·
[Group Coordination](#group-coordination) ·
[Display and Accessibility](#display-and-accessibility) ·
[Profiles and Diagnostics](#profiles-and-diagnostics)

### Live Buff Queue

| Feature | Controls and behavior |
|---|---|
| Discovery and eligibility | Checks group members, target, mouseover, and readable friendly nameplates for buffs you know that fit the recipient. Uses spell range where available and proximity where needed. `/br assumerange` lets you opt into listing players with unknown range. `/br rangewatch` can alert when someone who needs a buff enters range. |
| Safety and pauses | Combat hides and disarms cast rows and excludes targets in combat. Death and ghost state suspend the addon UI. Choose group-only visibility, major-city pauses, battleground and arena pauses, flight-path pauses, PvP skips, and a low-mana threshold with `/br group`, `/br cities`, `/br bg`, `/br taxi`, `/br pvp`, and `/br mana`. |
| Queue order | Check yourself first, prioritize recently resurrected players, and pin one player. Sort by name, tanks and leaders, distance, or most buffs needed. Filter by name or by group role when the client supplies roles. Use `/br self`, `/br pin`, `/br sort`, `/br find`, and `/br filter`. |
| List views | Use `/br view people\|buffs` for a row per player or per needed buff. The list fits up to 15 rows to the usable screen size. Scroll with the wheel or `/br scroll up\|down`; Cast Next Buff still uses the head of the full queue. |
| Ignore lists | Right-click a row to save an ignore or Shift-right-click to ignore for this session. Manage entries under **Ignore & Stats** or with `/br ignore`, `/br unignore`, `/br signore`, and `/br unsignore`. Export or import with `/br ignorelist export` or `/br ignorelist import`. The permanent list holds up to 192 names; imports past that limit do not partially apply. |
| Scan options | Queue refreshes are event-driven. `/br throttle on` adjusts the low-frequency cooldown sweep for movement, group size, and latency; it does not throttle aura or roster refresh events. `/br fastaura` skips rescans when a readable aura change can be identified as unrelated to watched buffs. |

### Casting

- **Four keybinds.** Cast next buff, cast next group buff, show or hide the
  window, and mute or unmute alerts. Open them with `/br key`.
- **Buff and rank selection.** Enable buffs individually, set priority with
  `/br prio`, and set a shared or per-buff rebuff threshold with `/br rebuff`.
  Group equivalents satisfy the same underlying buff. `/br smartprio on`
  can promote eligible buffs for tank or healer roles, wipe recovery, and
  saved instance rules. Manual priority breaks ties. BuffRadar skips spells
  on cooldown and can pick a recipient-eligible rank when the data is available.
- **Cast preview.** Hover a row or the window footer to see the planned cast.
  The next-cast tooltip can show the target, spell rank, fallback reason,
  and known group-blocker count. The footer also reports direct-binding
  and action-bar macro readiness separately. A populated queue does not
  mean that both delivery methods are armed. An unavailable or pending
  macro reports its reason; use **Cast next buff** only when that binding
  is shown as ready. `/br status export` includes the same **Cast delivery**
  diagnostics without changing the macro.
- **Group versions.** Set the minimum need for automatic group-cast offers
  with `/br groupcast`. Enable Shift-click with `/br modclick` and register
  your own spells with `/br grouppair "Single" "Group"`. BuffRadar falls
  back to a single-target cast when the roster, assignment, spell range,
  cooldown, or a required reagent blocks the group cast. Supported group pets
  get single-target buffs; they do not count toward the group-cast threshold.
- **Cast controls.** `/br mode` selects target, spell ID, macro, or ranked
  macro mode. `/br clickreg` chooses when clicks fire. If BuffRadar can tie
  a line-of-sight failure to its cast, it skips that target temporarily so
  the next cast can move on.

Plain-name macro mode leaves rank selection to the game. The other supported
cast modes use recipient-level rank information when available; missing rank
or level data can leave the highest learned rank as the fallback. Review the
next-cast preview when buffing lower-level players.

### Supported Buffs

The Buffs tab shows spells your character knows. These are the built-in
families. Use `/br buffs` for buff keys, `/br toggle <key>` to change a
toggle, and `/br context` to restrict a buff to raids or instances. Use
`/br custom add <spell ID>`, `/br custom remove <spell ID>`, and
`/br custom list` to manage custom watched buffs for the current character.

| Class | Enabled by Default | Optional |
|---|---|---|
| Druid | Mark of the Wild / Gift of the Wild, Thorns for melee classes | **Thorns: Any Class Outdoors** extends Thorns to all classes in the open world. Explicit assignments take precedence. |
| Priest | Power Word: Fortitude / Prayer of Fortitude, Divine Spirit / Prayer of Spirit for mana users, Fear Ward for warriors, Inner Fire, Shadowguard | Shadow Protection / Prayer of Shadow Protection |
| Mage | Arcane Intellect / Arcane Brilliance for mana users, Molten / Mage / Ice / Frost Armor | Dampen Magic, Amplify Magic |
| Paladin | One blessing per class. Kings when known, with Might for warriors and rogues and Wisdom for other classes as defaults when Kings is unavailable. | Aura watch |
| Shaman | Water Shield or Lightning Shield | Earth Shield for warriors, Water Breathing |
| Warlock | Fel Armor, Demon Armor, or Demon Skin | Unending Breath, Detect Invisibility and its Greater and Lesser variants |
| Hunter | | Aspect watch |

The Paladin planner supports Might, Wisdom, Kings, Salvation, Light, and
Sanctuary, including their learned Greater versions. Enable the Paladin
aura and Hunter aspect reminders with `/br aura`.

### Assignments

- **Blessings by Class.** Set your preferences with
  `/br bless prefer <class> <blessing|DEFAULT>`. An active group plan takes
  precedence over personal class preferences. Use
  `/br bless player <target|name> <blessing|DEFAULT>` for a normal blessing
  exception in your current group, subject to the plan's caster ownership.
  **Complement Nearby Blessings** is on by default: outside your group, it
  offers a different known blessing when another Paladin already provides
  your preferred one. Use `/br bless complement off` to turn it off.
  Explicit rules take precedence.
- **Class & Role Assignments.** Enable the table in **Settings → Buffs** or
  with `/br buffassign on`. It uses the class and known group role, or
  the class's **World** cell when the role is unavailable or the player is
  outside your group. Unset cells fall back to **All**, then the normal
  rules. Choose **None** to skip managed targeted buffs or **Default** to
  restore inheritance. Named profiles can save and share the table.
- **Preview Current Group.** Use `/br buffassign preview` to see each
  member's effective rule, available casts, and group blockers. Set a
  session role override when the game has supplied no role. The override
  clears when the player leaves or the UI reloads. `/br why <name>` shows
  the deciding rule and any role override.
- **Review blocker edits.** See which players and rules block a group cast,
  with incomplete roster information flagged. **Edit Rule** opens the
  exact assignment cell or blessing exception. **Review Changes** shows
  who would gain or lose buff offers, and **Apply** rechecks the roster
  and refreshes the blockers. `/br practice` uses a sample roster.
  `/br undo` reverses the last eligible blocker edit in the same session.

### Raid Tools and Reports

| Feature | Controls and behavior |
|---|---|
| Raid Coverage | `/br coverage` opens a read-only report of confirmed, missing, and unknown buffs by subgroup. Select a buff to drill down to the affected players. |
| Raid Preparation | Open the read-only checklist from **Raid Coverage** or use `/br prep`. Expand a player for missing and expiring buffs, consumable checks, and unknown readings. **Reagents** compares carried quantities with estimated needs and flags shortfalls. Roster changes refresh the open checklist and preserve expansion for a player still present. Open **Personal** with `/br readiness`, even solo, for food, flask, an optional consumable aura, carried Healthstones, durability, and applicable weapon and pet checks. |
| Subgroup Responsibilities | Open from **Raid Coverage** or `/br subgroup panel`. Restrict a buff to selected raid groups, preview the affected roster, and see why a group cast may fall back to a single-target cast. For example, `/br subgroup FORTITUDE 1,2` assigns groups 1 and 2. Set **All** or **None** as needed. Rules clear when you leave the raid or reload. |
| Ready Checks | `/br ready show` lists player responses, missing and expiring buffs, unknowns, and estimated group reagents. `/br readypost` lets leaders and assistants enable automatic group-chat summaries. |
| Recaps and sharing | Get a death recap or post-wipe rebuff report and reprint them with `/br death show` and `/br wipe show`. Use `/br summary` for needs by buff, `/br announce` requests a party or raid send and falls back to a local report on refusal; it cannot confirm delivery. `/br discord` copies Markdown. |
| Coverage line | Pick visible parts with `/br cover` including progress, buffs and cooldowns, the active or away BuffRadar roster, group expiry, world buffs, drinking healers, and session uptime. `/br uptime` reports the share of grouped scans that found every checked player buffed. |
| Encounter debuffs | In Settings → **Readiness**, or with `/br debuff add <spell ID> [player\|focus] [encounter ID]` and `/br debuff on`, show readable auras and their stacks in a separate strip. An encounter ID restricts a rule to that fight. |
| Extras to watch | Read recognised flask and food auras and see your temporary melee-weapon coating, and track your focus target's buff needs, world buff timers, or drinking healers. Watch group pets for Fortitude, Mark of the Wild, and Arcane Intellect. Use `/br consumables`, `/br weapon`, `/br focus`, `/br worldbuff`, `/br drink`, or `/br pets`. |

### Group Coordination

- **Caster Coordination.** Open from **Class & Role Assignments** or with
  `/br coordinate panel`, enable cast sync, and opt in for the group.
  Leaders and assistants can request reports of known spells, build and
  review a draft, publish duties, and track acknowledgements. Casters can
  review, accept, or decline an incoming plan. Acknowledgements are shown
  separately from buff coverage. Plans clear when the roster or leadership
  changes. The **Peers** tab shows verification, pending replies, retries,
  no response, and incompatible protocols independently of plan acceptance.
  Run `/br coordinate` for the available commands.
- **Cast sync and handoff.** `/br sync` shares successful cast status with
  other BuffRadar users in the group. `/br assign` lets leaders and
  assistants assign casters to buffs. Leaders, assistants, and Paladins can use
  `/br bless <class> <blessing> [caster]` to share a class blessing plan
  with optional ownership. `/br buddy` splits
  queues between active casters. Cover-me handoff redistributes duties
  when a participating caster dies or goes AFK.
- **Requests and reminders.** Tag eligible players who ask for buffs in
  nearby chat or whispers, print a joining-group digest, tag the next row
  after a cast, and remind yourself when you enter an instance unbuffed.
  Use `/br requests`, `/br digest`, and `/br enterflash` or open
  **Settings → Behavior**.
- **Alerts.** Choose droplet, system sound, or silence for new names,
  single-target buff drops, requests, and post-combat alerts for buffs that
  fell off during the fight.
  Test and silence alerts in instances from the **Alerts** tab. The
  window can flash after combat or for a supported pull countdown.
  See `/br soundfor`, `/br watch`, `/br fallsound`, and `/br pullflash`.
- **Expiry forecasts.** `/br forecast 60` warns about confirmed expirations
  within 60 seconds. A supported pull timer extends the window to include the
  countdown plus the lead time; `/br forecast timer 30` sets a local deadline.
  Use `/br forecast off` to disable notices. Forecasts do not infer boss
  mechanics or arm casts earlier than `/br rebuff` allows.

### Display and Accessibility

- **Window layout.** Drag, lock, resize from the bottom corners, reset
  position or appearance, and set width, list scale, or settings scale
  independently. Save position per character and scale per specialization.
  Use `/br positions on` to remember the Settings and Ready Check panels'
  positions separately (off by default); use `reset` to recenter them.
  Move the main window through the game's Edit Mode when available.
  Hold Shift to snap while resizing when enabled. Click-through while
  locked, idle fade, an all-buffed pill with click-to-peek, and empty-list
  hiding are optional. Hover to show the close button. Hiding the title
  frees the header space.
- **Rows and styling.** Choose compact rows, two columns, upward growth,
  text size, row spacing, and icon size. Customize background color,
  opacity, border, and themes. Choose a built-in palette or save up to four
  custom themes. Select **Auto** to match a loaded UI addon, then open
  **Auto Theme Priority** on the Window tab to reorder matches and see the
  selected addon. The Theme button or `/br theme preview` previews palettes
  before saving; **Apply** saves the choice and **Cancel** restores the look.
  Show class colors, realm names,
  raid markers, duration bars, or colored marks for tanks, assignments,
  expiry, and the buddy split. Trim long names and select minimal,
  standard, or full tooltips with buff durations where available.
- **Quick controls.** Toggle known buffs from the icon strip, add a name
  finder to the list, and show or hide the cast counter. Open settings
  from the gear icon, the movable minimap button, the add-on menu
  where available, or `/br config`. The minimap marks confirmed coverage
  green (`+`), ordinary needs yellow (`!`), critical needs red (`!!`), and
  unknown coverage gray (`?`). A paused scan has no mark. `/br visual on`
  adds quiet highlights independently of sound and respects Reduced Motion.
- **Accessible settings.** Search every tab with `/br config find`. Results
  show their destination tab and setting, including unavailable controls.
  The six tabs are **Window**, **Alerts**, **Buffs**, **Behavior**,
  **Ignore & Stats**, and **Readiness**. Use
  `/br config navigate` for keyboard controls or `/br config narrate`
  for the game's configured text-to-speech voice. Tab or Shift+Tab moves,
  Enter or Space activates, arrow keys adjust, F1 toggles speech, and
  Escape exits navigation. The color picker, keybind prompt, setup wizard,
  and profile share dialogs have their own controls. Enable status symbols
  with `/br tagsymbols` and reduced motion with `/br motion`.
- **Languages.** English plus complete German, French, Spanish, Russian and
  Simplified Chinese packs cover all current interface strings. Offline checks
  verify keys, format contracts and locale-first flows; native-speaker and
  actual client rendering review remain separate.

### Profiles and Diagnostics

Use `/br firstcast` for a session-local guide through discovery and cast readiness.
It waits for a cast you activate through the existing list, binding or managed
macro, and confirms only an attributed success. It never casts automatically.
`/br support` opens a local copy window with allowlisted technical settings,
aggregate counts, readiness, categorized errors, peer verification counts,
and the selected theme. It also reports instance type, pause preferences,
combat/PvP state and detected blessing families from the current spell cache.
Unknown readings are marked unknown. It excludes player names,
profile labels, history, macro text and raw errors, and sends nothing. Both
actions are available in the **Readiness** settings tab.

For battleground or blessing questions, use `/br why NAME` on a visible friendly
player. It explains the current pause separately from that player's buff needs,
and distinguishes a preferred blessing from the effective choice and any
assignment, plan, preference or complement rule. Detected blessings are shown
separately from class defaults. The output stays local in chat.

| Feature | Controls and behavior |
|---|---|
| Presets and specialization | Quick Setup drafts a preset and alert preferences based on your activity and role. It applies them only on confirmation. Standalone presets are available through `/br preset`. Buff toggles and rebuff overrides can follow the active specialization when the client identifies it. |
| Named profiles | Save, load, list, delete, and share profiles from **Ignore & Stats** or `/br profile`. Preview a saved profile's differences with `/br profile diff <name>`. `/br autoprofile` can switch profiles for raids, dungeons, battlegrounds, grouped world play, or solo play. |
| Import and export | `/br import` reviews a legacy BR1 settings copy before applying it locally. `/br profile import` previews a named profile; rename it or confirm replacement, then load it separately. `/br plan import` reviews a plan and defaults to applying locally. **Apply and share** requires current group authority and sync, and sends only changed assignments and blessings, never auto-profile mappings. |
| Casts and history | Show session and all-time totals, reset counters, see per-spell stats or export them, and review the last 50 tracked casts. See `/br count`, `/br resetcount`, `/br stats`, and `/br history`. `/br offenders` tracks up to 50 records by player identity, counted once per group session. |
| Troubleshooting | `/br why <name>` explains how a player is handled. `/br debug` reports client and window state, `/br clicks` logs cast attempts, `/br selftest` prints a report for bug reports, `/br apicheck export` produces a copyable API report, `/br buffcheck` checks spell IDs, and `/br perf` reports separate scan, preparation, import and debuff CPU timings when available. `/br stats memory` reports the game's addon total, not per-feature estimates. `/br lite on` pauses forecasts, readiness, debuffs, and optional watches without changing their saved settings. |
| UI integration and feedback | Use the [read-only status API](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/docs/STATUS_API.md) or `/br status export`. Get a copyable feature-request link with `/br feedback` or see the [roadmap](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md). |

## Player Guides

Find supported buffs, settings, and commands in the
[Forever Player Guide](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/editions/forever/README.md). Review release details in
the [Changelog](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/editions/forever/CHANGELOG.md).

BuffRadar has targeted Forever since 1.8.0. The last Retail release was
1.7.0. See the [Retail Guide](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/README.md) and
[Support Decision](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/docs/DECISIONS.md#2026-10-25--retail-support-dropped-forever-only-from-180-sean).

## Source and Contributions

The [Forever TOC](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/editions/forever/BuffRadar.toc) and the historical
[Retail TOC](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/BuffRadar.toc) load a shared Lua 5.1 implementation:

- [Data](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Data.lua) checks the client using the shipping TOC marker.
  [SavedVariables](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/SavedVariables.lua) validates and migrates
  `BuffRadarDB` on a detached copy; [Profiles](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Profiles.lua)
  handles settings and plan imports and exports.
- [Core](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/BuffRadar.lua) scans and builds the cast queue.
  [Intelligence](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Intelligence.lua) owns adaptive cooldown-sweep cadence,
  forecasts and contextual priority. [Status](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Status.lua) publishes copies;
  [Debuffs](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Debuffs.lua) and [Readiness](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Readiness.lua)
  own optional aura and inventory checks.
  [Coordination](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Coordination.lua) handles group messages and plans.
- [Window](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Window.lua) owns the main window and secure buttons.
  [Minimap](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Minimap.lua) owns the minimap and addon menu.
  [Config](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Config.lua), [Wizard](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Wizard.lua), and
  [Slash](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/BuffRadar/Slash.lua) handle settings, setup, and commands.

- [Report a bug or request a feature](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/issues/new/choose).
  Use the [security policy](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for private reports.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [local checks](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/tools/README.md).

## Repository Layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `BuffRadar/` | Shared addon source, translations, art, bindings, and historical Retail files |
| `editions/forever/` | The Forever edition's `.toc`, README and changelog |
| `build.ps1`, `tools/package.sh` | PowerShell 7 and POSIX entry points to the same deterministic Forever packager |
| `tools/` | Automated checks — see [tools/README.md](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/tools/README.md) |
| `.luacheckrc` | luacheck settings used by the checks |
| `AGENTS.md` | Project rule sheet (prompt in force, frozen foundation, gate) |
| `QUALITY.md` | Quality scorecard, scored from evidence |
| `docs/` | Capability matrix, decision log, status API, and roadmap |
| `SECURITY.md` | How to report a security problem, privately |

## Making a Release

Run `sh tools/gate.sh` on POSIX (Python 3.10+ with Lupa) and Luacheck 1.2.0
on `BuffRadar/`, or use `tools/check.ps1` in PowerShell 7 (`-Setup` once).
Build with `sh tools/package.sh` or `./build.ps1`. Both write the Forever ZIP
and `SHA256SUMS.txt` to `dist/`. With the gate's Python environment active, run:

```sh
python -I tools/checkpackage.py dist/BuffRadar-X.Y.Z-Forever.zip .
```

Replace `X.Y.Z` with the TOC version. In CI the Windows and POSIX digests
must match. Test the exact ZIP in Forever with the
[release checklist](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/docs/FOREVER_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md), not a loose source
copy. Record the digest, game build and results. See the
[audit ledger](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/BuffRadar/blob/main/docs/AUDIT_1.15.38.md) for offline coverage and limits.
After a tagged release, verify the hosted ZIP against its published checksum
and the tested artifact.

releases.name: BuffRadar 1.20.2
releases.notes:
## 1.20.2 — WoW: Forever

- Enable nearby blessing complement by default, so another Paladin's Kings
  can be replaced by an available class-appropriate blessing such as Might.
- Migrate existing settings to the new default; use
  `/br bless complement off` to opt out.

releases.name: BuffRadar 1.20.1
releases.notes:
## 1.20.1 — WoW: Forever

- Clarify that queue refreshes are event-driven while the low-frequency
  cooldown-readiness sweep remains an adaptive fallback.
- Add an explicit verification report separating automated fake-client results
  from live-client testing, which remains unperformed for this release.
- Improve the settings label and help for `/br throttle`; no casting or pause
  behavior is changed by this documentation-focused update.

releases.name: BuffRadar 1.20.0
releases.notes:
## 1.20.0 — WoW: Forever

- Replace recurring polling with event-driven refreshes where supported, and
  expose read-only status for integrations through the display bridge.
- Harden combat, death, and protected-action handling; settings and display
  changes now respect client lockdown and recover from delayed life-state flags.
- Add Auto Theme Priority controls and preserve modal editors during live
  settings refreshes.
- Expand offline coverage for timer variants, fallback UI templates, combat
  transitions, and configuration panels.

releases.name: BuffRadar 1.19.1
releases.notes:
## 1.19.1 — WoW: Forever

- Add battleground, pause-setting, combat and PvP safety details to the private
  Support report and local player explanations.
- Show detected blessings separately from the preferred blessing, and explain
  which assignment, plan or preference selected the offer.
- Explain when blessing complement applies, why it is suppressed, and when an
  unreadable aura or caster prevents a confident choice.
- Cover diagnostic privacy, unknown API results and isolation from scan state
  with offline regression checks.

releases.name: BuffRadar 1.19.0
releases.notes:
## 1.19.0 — WoW: Forever

- Find advanced actions alongside settings in search, or browse them from
  Actions. See the matching slash command and why an action is unavailable.
- Open Actions from Settings, `/br actions`, an optional keybind, or
  Shift-left-click on the gear. Ordinary gear clicks keep their existing uses.
- Open existing inspection, assignment, profile, and troubleshooting screens
  without memorizing commands. Keyboard navigation and narration remain available.
- Preview window themes before applying them. Cancel restores the previous
  appearance; Apply creates one undoable preference change.
- See peer verification, waiting replies, retries, and protocol mismatches in
  Caster Coordination, separately from plan acceptance and buff coverage.
- Include safe error counts, peer totals, and theme details in the local Support
  report, with player names, raw errors, and user text excluded.
- Add offline restart tests for settings, macros, bindings, queue recipients,
  and Auto themes using independent Lua clients.
